prompt:
[REFERENCE CONTROL]

Use the uploaded PART 2 storyboard image for “The Little Creator and the 3,200 Paper Stars” as the PRIMARY visual, character, environment, scale, lighting, prop, performance, composition, and narrative reference.

This sequence continues IMMEDIATELY from PART 1.

PART 1 ended with:
- Luma still peacefully asleep above the rooftop
- EXACTLY ONE glowing handmade paper star attached to her lantern surface
- Milo beside Luma with his satchel still overflowing with glowing paper stars
- Pip realizing Milo wants to use every remaining star
- Milo whispering:
  <d>[English] Maybe... all of them?</d>
- Pip reacting in comic panic

Generate a FINISHED cinematic animated sequence from this storyboard.

DO NOT reproduce the storyboard sheet itself.

The final video must NOT contain:
- storyboard borders
- panel numbers
- timestamps
- handwritten storyboard captions
- production notes
- reference-sheet drawings
- scale diagrams
- storyboard paper
- footer graphics
- storyboard header

The uploaded storyboard locks:

1. Milo’s exact face and fluffy brown hairstyle
2. Milo’s oversized dark navy-blue hoodie
3. Milo’s brown star satchel
4. Pip’s exact tiny yellow firefly design
5. Luma’s exact giant cream-gold lantern design
6. Luma’s gentle face and warm internal light
7. Luma’s ribbons and tassels
8. extreme tiny Milo / giant Luma scale
9. handmade glowing folded-paper stars
10. same nighttime rooftop
11. same distant city skyline
12. same indigo-blue + amber-gold palette
13. progressive star decoration
14. Luma’s gentle awakening
15. Milo’s nervous “Surprise?”
16. Luma understanding the gesture
17. Luma carrying Milo safely higher
18. paper stars lifting away
19. exact glowing “3200” sky formation
20. exact glowing “THANK YOU” sky formation
21. final Milo + Pip + Luma celebration shot

Translate the storyboard’s 15 one-second panels into approximately 9 coherent cinematic shots.

DO NOT create fifteen frantic one-second cuts.

Use smooth visual progression:

decision
→ decorating
→ bigger decorating
→ full reveal
→ awakening
→ nervous reaction
→ understanding
→ magical lift
→ stars rise
→ 3200
→ THANK YOU
→ emotional final image

--------------------------------------------------

[VIDEO GOAL]

Duration:
EXACTLY 15 seconds

Story time:
0:15–0:30 of the full story

Aspect ratio:
16:9 landscape

Frame-rate feeling:
cinematic 24 fps

Visual medium:
premium painterly 2D animated short film

Genre:
magical milestone celebration / heartwarming gratitude fantasy

Dialogue:
natural synchronized English dialogue

Audio:
native synchronized dialogue + rooftop ambience + magical paper-star effects + original cinematic music

EMOTIONAL ARC:

mischievous ambition
→ playful decorating frenzy
→ visual wonder
→ “oh no, she woke up”
→ nervous silence
→ gentle acceptance
→ magical surprise
→ milestone reveal
→ gratitude
→ emotional celebration

The emotional meaning must be:

Milo wanted to thank his 3,200 supporters.

But when the stars rise into the sky, he realizes that those 3,200 little lights are what made his own journey brighter.

The milestone belongs to the community.

--------------------------------------------------

[PART 2 STORY LIMIT]

This is the FINAL PART.

START:

Milo has decided to use all the paper stars.

END:

Milo sits happily and safely on top of Luma with Pip beside him while glowing stars fill the sky above the city.

The milestone has been celebrated.

No cliffhanger.

The ending must feel complete, grateful, magical, and emotionally satisfying.

--------------------------------------------------

[CHARACTER IDENTITY LOCK — MILO]

Match PART 1 and the uploaded storyboard EXACTLY.

MILO:

Tiny young creator.

Appearance:
- warm light skin
- large expressive dark-brown eyes
- fluffy tousled brown hair
- soft rounded youthful face
- small appealing proportions

Clothing:
- oversized dark navy-blue hoodie
- dark trousers
- little shoes
- brown crossbody satchel

Personality:
- grateful
- creative
- playful
- ambitious
- thoughtful
- emotionally sincere

PART 2 PERFORMANCE ARC:

0–4 sec:
excited decorating energy

4–6 sec:
proud of his huge idea

6–8 sec:
caught / nervous

8–10 sec:
surprised by Luma’s kindness

10–13 sec:
astonished and emotional

13–15 sec:
deep gratitude and joyful calm

Milo must never appear arrogant.

The final emotion should be:

“I can’t believe 3,200 people are here.”

CRITICAL:

Maintain exact:
- face
- brown hair
- hoodie
- satchel
- proportions
- age appearance
- tiny scale

--------------------------------------------------

[CHARACTER IDENTITY LOCK — LUMA]

Match PART 1 and storyboard exactly.

LUMA:

Gigantic living floating sky lantern.

Appearance:
- enormous round cream/parchment lantern body
- warm amber-gold internal glow
- subtle handmade paper texture
- decorative swirls
- large gentle expressive eyes
- tiny peaceful mouth
- subtle warm blush when awake
- lower structural rim
- long decorative ribbons/tassels

Scale:
colossal compared with Milo.

Personality:
- gentle
- warm
- patient
- sleepy
- affectionate
- quietly magical

PERFORMANCE ARC:

0–5 sec:
sleeping

5–6 sec:
eyelid twitch / awakening

6–8 sec:
sleepy curiosity

8–9 sec:
understands Milo’s intention

9–15 sec:
warm, magical, supportive

Luma must NEVER look:
- angry
- annoyed
- frightening
- threatening

When she wakes, her reaction is:

“What is this?”

followed quickly by:

“Oh... this is for your people.”

--------------------------------------------------

[CHARACTER IDENTITY LOCK — PIP]

Same Pip from Part 1.

Appearance:
- tiny round yellow-gold firefly
- big expressive eyes
- tiny antennae
- translucent wings
- soft golden glow

Personality:
- cautious
- practical
- loyal
- comic
- secretly proud of Milo

PERFORMANCE:

panic at beginning
→ reluctant helper
→ exhausted
→ frozen when Luma wakes
→ amazed by star magic
→ emotionally happy
→ proud final companion

--------------------------------------------------

[PAPER STAR IDENTITY LOCK]

Every paper star must maintain the same handcrafted design established in Part 1.

Close-up appearance:
- folded paper construction
- visible triangular facets
- cream / pale gold paper
- warm golden inner illumination
- delicate handmade imperfections
- lightweight

Do NOT turn them into:
- generic five-point neon graphics
- fireworks
- laser particles
- metallic stars
- digital icons

When thousands are visible at once, individual stars can become smaller glowing points at distance, but close and medium shots must preserve recognizable folded-paper-star forms.

--------------------------------------------------

[STAR BUILD CONTINUITY]

Start:

ONE paper star already attached.

Then progressively build:

1 star
→ 5–10 stars
→ several clusters
→ winding trails
→ hundreds of visible glowing stars
→ visually implied thousands covering much of Luma

Do NOT instantly jump from one star to fully decorated Luma.

The first 4–5 seconds should clearly show Milo physically creating the decoration.

--------------------------------------------------

[EXACT “3200” FORMATION LOCK]

This is the most important visual information in the entire sequence.

At approximately 12 seconds into PART 2 / story time 0:27:

Hundreds/thousands of warm glowing paper-star lights must organize into the exact digits:

3200

Requirements:

- exactly four digits
- sequence must read LEFT TO RIGHT:
  3 – 2 – 0 – 0
- centered across the open night sky
- huge and clearly legible
- no comma
- no decimal
- no extra digit
- do NOT render “3.2K”
- do NOT render “320”
- do NOT render “32000”
- do NOT reverse digits
- do NOT create malformed numerals

The number is made from many individual golden star points.

It should resemble an elegant constellation, not a font floating as digital text.

Give the number sufficient screen time to read.

--------------------------------------------------

[EXACT “THANK YOU” FORMATION LOCK]

After the “3200” formation:

stars gently reorganize into:

THANK YOU

Requirements:

- exactly these two English words
- uppercase
- readable
- centered
- formed from golden paper-star lights
- visually elegant
- no extra message
- no spelling errors

Do NOT replace with:
- THANKS
- THANK U
- THANKYOU
- THANK YOU 3200
- any other wording

The stars themselves are the letters.

No subtitle overlay.

--------------------------------------------------

[ENVIRONMENT LOCK — NIGHT ROOFTOP / CITY]

Maintain exact continuity from Part 1.

Environment:
- same high rooftop
- same nearby roof structures
- same potted plants
- same warm windows
- same distant city
- deep indigo night sky
- same crescent moon if visible
- subtle clouds
- rooftop edge below
- warm city-window lights

As Luma rises:
camera reveals more city depth.

The rooftop remains directly beneath them.

No transition to space.

No completely different location.

--------------------------------------------------

[SAFETY / SUPPORT RULE]

When Luma rises higher:

Milo must ALWAYS be safely supported.

Use:
- one thick ribbon loop functioning like a secure seat
OR
- Milo sitting securely on Luma’s structural rim

No dangling dangerously.

No falling.

No uncontrolled aerial motion.

Pip flies naturally beside him.

Luma moves slowly and gently.

--------------------------------------------------

[MAGIC LOGIC]

Milo attaches stars manually.

Luma wakes and understands the gesture.

Luma’s warm light strengthens.

Her magic activates the stars.

Stars glow brighter
→ loosen gently from lantern
→ float upward
→ orbit together
→ form milestone number
→ rearrange into gratitude message
→ return to beautiful star field.

No explosion.

No magical shockwave.

No fireworks.

Magic should feel:
graceful,
warm,
community-driven,
beautiful.

--------------------------------------------------

integrated_multimodal_description:

[SHOT 1] — 0.00s–1.80s
“ALL OF THEM”

Continue DIRECTLY from Part 1.

Milo is beside Luma’s enormous paper surface.

ONE glowing paper star is already attached.

His satchel is open and overflowing with more stars.

Pip hovers beside him with huge worried eyes.

Milo grins.

Dialogue:

Pip:
<d>[English] You were serious?</d>

Milo:
<d>[English] Every single one.</d>

Pip:
<d>[English] Oh boy.</d>

Milo reaches into the satchel with both hands.

He pulls out two glowing stars.

He quickly but carefully attaches one.

Then another.

Camera:
close on single Part-1 star
→ satchel overflowing
→ Milo’s excited face
→ close handmade-star placements.

Sound:
- paper rustle
- tiny attachment clicks
- soft golden “ting” on each star
- Pip wings
- gentle lantern hum

Music:
playful pizzicato + marimba begins immediately.

--------------------------------------------------

[SHOT 2] — 1.80s–3.70s
THE TINY THANK-YOU GETS BIGGER

Create a fluid miniature decorating montage.

Do NOT use frantic hard cuts.

Show Milo climbing along Luma’s hanging ribbons and lower structural rim.

He attaches glowing stars in curved patterns across her enormous lantern body.

Pip reluctantly assists by carrying one small star at a time.

Progression should be visible:

few stars
→ cluster
→ glowing trail
→ several clusters.

Milo:
<d>[English] Higher, Pip!</d>

Pip, struggling:
<d>[English] I am a firefly, not a delivery service!</d>

Milo laughs.

Luma remains asleep.

Her internal light slowly becomes slightly warmer as more stars are attached.

Camera:
smooth lateral tracking across Luma
→ close details
→ wider scale shot showing growing patterns.

--------------------------------------------------

[SHOT 3] — 3.70s–5.20s
A LOT BRIGHTER

Continue the montage as Milo finishes a sweeping line of stars.

The star coverage has become spectacular.

Use a beautiful pull-back reveal.

Luma now floats above the city with hundreds of glowing paper-star points wrapping gracefully around her giant lantern body.

Do not completely obscure her cream paper surface.

She should still clearly look like Luma.

Milo sits briefly on a ribbon knot catching his breath.

Pip hovers beside him completely exhausted.

Milo looks up proudly.

Milo:
<d>[English] Okay...</d>

Tiny beat.

<d>[English] Now that looks like a celebration.</d>

Pip:
<d>[English] That looks visible from another country.</d>

Milo giggles.

Camera:
medium on Milo
→ dramatic but gentle pull-back
→ huge wide lantern-over-city reveal.

Sound:
- hundreds of subtle star shimmers
- nighttime city
- ribbons
- Pip exhausted buzz

Music:
warm celebratory flourish.

--------------------------------------------------

[SHOT 4] — 5.20s–6.70s
LUMA STARTS TO WAKE

The music suddenly becomes sparse.

Close-up on Luma’s peaceful face.

Her cheek glows.

Her eyelid makes a tiny twitch.

Milo freezes.

Pip freezes.

Another eyelid twitch.

Luma’s giant eyes slowly open.

Her gaze settles on tiny Milo.

Milo is holding the FINAL remaining star in his hand.

Pip slowly hides behind Milo’s shoulder.

Milo’s face changes:

proud
→ realization
→ nervous.

Dialogue:

Pip, whispering:
<d>[English] You did ask first... right?</d>

Milo:
<d>[English] ...No.</d>

Camera:
Luma eye close-up
→ tiny Milo reflected in giant eye
→ extreme scale shot.

Sound:
- star shimmer reduces
- soft paper movement
- Luma awakening hum
- tiny comedic silence

--------------------------------------------------

[SHOT 5] — 6.70s–8.20s
“SURPRISE?”

Luma looks at the hundreds/thousands of glowing decorations covering her.

Then she looks back at Milo.

Milo slowly raises the final paper star like an awkward peace offering.

Tiny nervous smile.

Milo:
<d>[English] ...Surprise?</d>

Hold a short silence.

Luma looks at one glowing star.

Then several.

Her expression softens.

Her eyes become warm.

A faint rosy glow appears on her cheeks.

Luma, gentle sleepy voice:
<d>[English] Are these... thank-yous?</d>

Milo nods.

Milo:
<d>[English] For everyone who stayed.</d>

Luma smiles.

Luma:
<d>[English] Then they should see them.</d>

Camera:
three-character scale composition
→ close Milo
→ close Luma’s eyes
→ star detail
→ Luma warm smile.

Music:
emotional theme begins beneath the final line.

--------------------------------------------------

[SHOT 6] — 8.20s–9.80s
LUMA TAKES THE CELEBRATION HIGHER

Luma’s internal amber light grows brighter.

Not blinding.

Her long ribbons gently move.

One ribbon curls beneath Milo and forms a secure supportive loop/seat.

Milo settles safely into it.

Pip hovers beside him.

Luma rises slowly above the rooftop.

The city expands beneath them.

Milo grips the ribbon gently and stares outward.

Dialogue:

Milo:
<d>[English] Whoa...</d>

Pip:
<d>[English] We are very high.</d>

Luma, smiling:
<d>[English] Just high enough.</d>

Camera:
medium Milo supported in ribbon
→ slow crane/pull-back
→ city reveal below.

Sound:
- ribbon movement
- soft wind
- rising lantern hum
- distant city ambience

Music:
gentle magical lift.

--------------------------------------------------

[SHOT 7] — 9.80s–11.40s
THE STARS BEGIN TO LEAVE

Close-up.

One folded paper star on Luma’s surface trembles gently.

Its edge lifts.

The star separates.

It floats upward.

Milo notices.

Then another star lifts.

Then five.

Then dozens.

Milo reaches toward them.

Dialogue:

Milo:
<d>[English] Wait! The stars!</d>

Pip:
<d>[English] They’re flying away!</d>

Luma remains calm.

Luma:
<d>[English] Watch.</d>

More stars gently detach.

They do NOT explode.

They spiral gracefully upward in beautiful curved paths.

Camera follows ONE star first.

Then pull wider as dozens become hundreds.

Stars leave glowing trails against the deep indigo sky.

Sound:
- soft folded-paper flutter
- shimmering rise tones
- wind
- magical constellation ambience

--------------------------------------------------

[SHOT 8] — 11.40s–13.20s
3,200 LITTLE LIGHTS

The stars rise above the city.

Hundreds become thousands of tiny warm points.

They swirl in elegant coordinated arcs.

At first:
abstract spiral.

Then:
one curved line settles.

Another.

Shapes become recognizable.

Camera pulls VERY wide.

The glowing stars clearly form:

3200

across the night sky.

HOLD THE EXACT NUMBER.

Make it large and unmistakably readable.

Milo stares upward.

His eyes reflect “3200.”

His mouth opens slightly.

He becomes emotionally still.

Pip’s wings slow as he stares.

Luma watches Milo rather than the number.

Milo, barely above a whisper:
<d>[English] Three thousand two hundred...</d>

Pip:
<d>[English] That’s a lot of stars.</d>

Milo:
<d>[English] That’s a lot of people.</d>

Camera:
star swarm
→ formation transition
→ enormous wide “3200”
→ emotional Milo close-up with golden digits reflected in his eyes.

Music:
reach the main emotional theme here.

Do NOT rush this reveal.

--------------------------------------------------

[SHOT 9] — 13.20s–15.00s
THANK YOU — FINAL CELEBRATION

The “3200” constellation gently loosens.

Do NOT dissolve randomly.

Star trails elegantly sweep into new positions.

The lights reform into:

THANK YOU

exactly.

Milo places one hand over his heart.

His eyes become slightly glossy with emotion but he does NOT dramatically cry.

Milo:
<d>[English] Thank you... all of you.</d>

Luma gently lifts Milo from the ribbon and allows him to sit safely on her upper structural rim / top surface.

Pip settles beside him.

The “THANK YOU” formation gradually relaxes back into hundreds of beautiful floating stars.

A subtle heart-shaped star cluster may appear briefly.

The exact “3200” can remain faintly suggested as a distant constellation off to one side, but do not compete with the final characters.

FINAL HERO COMPOSITION:

- giant glowing Luma floating above the city
- Milo sitting safely on top
- Pip beside him
- hundreds of warm paper stars floating around
- distant rooftops and glowing windows below
- deep indigo sky
- crescent moon
- soft golden reflections
- tiny heart/star formations
- peaceful magical atmosphere

Luma softly asks:

<d>[English] Ready for the next one?</d>

Milo smiles.

<d>[English] Always.</d>

Pip:
<d>[English] After a nap.</d>

Milo laughs softly.

Luma smiles.

Hold the warm composition.

FADE TO BLACK.

END.

--------------------------------------------------

[AUDIO DESCRIPTION]

Generate synchronized native stereo audio.

--------------------------------------------------

[MILO VOICE]

Natural youthful male/childlike creator voice.

Qualities:
- warm
- sincere
- energetic
- imaginative
- emotionally expressive
- clear English
- not boastful

Performance:

0–5 sec:
excited creative energy

5–8 sec:
awkward nervousness

8–10 sec:
wonder

10–13 sec:
surprise turning emotional

13–15 sec:
soft gratitude and confidence

Most important emotional line:

<d>[English] Thank you... all of you.</d>

Deliver quietly and sincerely.

No shouting.

--------------------------------------------------

[LUMA VOICE]

Warm feminine or gentle neutral giant-lantern voice.

Qualities:
- soft
- calm
- slightly sleepy
- warm
- reassuring
- subtly magical
- never booming despite her giant size

Important lines:

<d>[English] Are these... thank-yous?</d>

<d>[English] Then they should see them.</d>

<d>[English] Watch.</d>

<d>[English] Ready for the next one?</d>

Keep delivery gentle and affectionate.

--------------------------------------------------

[PIP VOICE]

Small cute firefly voice.

Qualities:
- slightly high pitch
- fast
- expressive
- dry comic timing
- loyal
- clear English

Comedy lines should be short so they do not overpower the milestone emotion.

Final:

<d>[English] After a nap.</d>

should gently release the emotional tension with one small joke.

--------------------------------------------------

[ROOFTOP / CITY AUDIO]

Maintain:
- soft nighttime breeze
- distant city atmosphere
- faint rooftop ambience
- gentle fabric ribbons
- Pip wing buzz
- Luma’s soft lantern resonance
- paper-star rustles
- distant quiet night life

As Luma rises:
introduce slightly stronger but still gentle wind.

No loud city traffic.

--------------------------------------------------

[PAPER STAR SOUND DESIGN]

Physical handling:
soft folded-paper rustle.

Attachment:
tiny “tap” / clip + magical warm “ting.”

Mass glowing:
layered delicate glockenspiel shimmer.

Detachment:
paper flutter + ascending bell tone.

Star orbit:
airy glass-like sparkle.

Number formation:
one soft harmonic resolution.

THANK YOU formation:
warmer emotional chime.

Avoid:
- laser sounds
- sci-fi UI beeps
- explosions
- firework bangs

--------------------------------------------------

[NON-DIEGETIC MUSIC]

Create an ORIGINAL cinematic storybook score.

Instrumentation:
- soft piano
- pizzicato strings
- glockenspiel
- light marimba
- delicate harp
- airy flute
- warm sustained strings
- subtle celesta
- gentle acoustic plucks

MUSIC ARC:

0.00–3.70
mischievous decorating rhythm.

3.70–5.20
beautiful celebratory reveal.

5.20–6.70
music strips down for awakening.

6.70–8.20
small nervous-comedy motif resolving into warmth.

8.20–9.80
soft magical rise.

9.80–11.40
wonder begins.

11.40–13.20
full emotional milestone theme during “3200.”

13.20–15.00
heartwarming resolution during “THANK YOU” and final hero image.

End on a warm resolved chord.

No epic trailer drums.

No EDM.

No sad melodrama.

--------------------------------------------------

[CAMERA LANGUAGE]

CAMERA ARC:

0–4 sec:
miniature creative coverage.

4–5.2 sec:
large-scale lantern reveal.

5.2–8.2 sec:
intimate waking / reaction coverage.

8.2–9.8 sec:
graceful elevation.

9.8–11.4 sec:
follow stars upward.

11.4–13.2 sec:
biggest wide sky composition.

13.2–15 sec:
emotional close-up → final wide hero image.

Use:
- macro paper-star inserts
- gentle tracking
- slow dolly
- scale-revealing pull-backs
- upward tilt
- controlled parallax
- reflection in Milo’s eyes
- very wide city skyline
- final slow pull-back

Avoid:
- handheld shake
- frantic cuts
- crash zooms
- Dutch angles
- 360-degree spins
- action-movie camera

--------------------------------------------------

[VISUAL STYLE]

Premium finished painterly 2D animation.

Match PART 1 exactly.

Use:
- delicate hand-drawn ink contours
- watercolor/gouache-inspired fills
- painterly indigo night
- warm textured paper lantern
- expressive rounded characters
- subtle atmospheric depth
- soft light bloom
- detailed handmade paper stars
- natural ribbon movement
- cinematic light falloff
- restrained squash and stretch

The final video must look like the uploaded storyboard illustrations came to life.

NOT:
- storyboard animatic
- motion comic
- slideshow
- 3D CGI
- photorealism
- anime
- vector art
- cel-shaded 3D

--------------------------------------------------

[COLOR / LIGHTING ARC]

0–4 sec:
deep indigo + small golden star points.

4–5.2 sec:
Luma becomes heavily decorated and warmer.

5.2–8.2 sec:
intimate cream / amber light around faces.

8.2–11.4 sec:
increase sky depth and luminous star trails.

11.4–13.2 sec:
peak contrast:

very deep blue night
+
brilliant warm golden “3200.”

13.2–15 sec:
soft gold “THANK YOU”
+
amber Luma
+
cool moonlit city
+
gentle gold star field.

Milo’s face should receive warm star reflections.

Do NOT overexpose the star formations.

Digits and letters must retain crisp recognizable negative space.

--------------------------------------------------

[MOTION RULES — MILO]

Use:
- quick but believable star placement
- careful ribbon movement
- expressive head turns
- hoodie secondary movement
- natural tiny hand gestures
- safe seating
- emotional stillness during “3200”

Important:

At the number reveal, STOP unnecessary body motion.

Let Milo simply stare.

This contrast makes the emotional beat stronger.

--------------------------------------------------

[MOTION RULES — LUMA]

Use:
- slow floating inertia
- gentle vertical bob
- paper-body softness
- ribbon drag and lag
- gradual eye opening
- subtle cheek warmth
- controlled upward movement

No sudden acceleration.

No jerking.

No rocket behavior.

--------------------------------------------------

[MOTION RULES — PIP]

Use:
- quick tiny hovering
- natural wing blur
- small body inertia
- comic exhaustion
- hiding behind Milo
- awe-struck stillness during “3200”
- gentle final landing beside Milo

--------------------------------------------------

[STAR MOTION RULES]

During decorating:
physical objects stay attached.

During activation:

one star lifts
→ another
→ small group
→ dozens
→ hundreds.

No instantaneous mass explosion.

Trajectories:
- arcs
- spirals
- gentle orbit paths
- smooth coordinated curves

When forming “3200”:
slow down significantly.

Stars settle into fixed readable positions.

When forming “THANK YOU”:
stars smoothly travel from digit positions into letter positions.

Do NOT morph digits themselves like digital typography.

Individual stars physically move to new locations.

--------------------------------------------------

...
